content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I wanted to ask if it's possible to connect a device to [product_name] and record all analog and digital inputs and outputs. I'm aiming to set up a 24 or 48 hour logging session to analyze my solar hot water heating system, capturing data that isn't visible directly on the [product_name] display. If this has already been discussed, could you point me to the relevant thread?

Hello, You can find solutions in the German section of the forum under PC-Logger-software. Take a look at the responses and attachments from the users "ASK" and "Superbrudi". Also, check the topic about [product_name] as a Modbus device. Best regards, [user_name]

Thank you, [user_name]. This is a great help! I used Google Translate for the German instructions and found the solution. People I asked previously said it wasn't possible. I'll test the software and share my experiences. Best regards, [user_name]

Hello everyone, Following [user_name]'s suggestion, I've downloaded LogoLog for data logging from the German forum, but I'm having trouble starting it. With [product_name] running and connected to PC COM1, I open DOS, copy LogoLog1 into a folder, and run it. However, after starting the program, I get no prompt for values, just "LogoLog1 Filename Interval[min]" then back to the directory prompt. Has anyone managed to use this DOS logger successfully lately? Any advice appreciated. Thanks in advance. [user_name]

Hello [user_name], Please try this: 1. Create a file called "solar.csv" (name can vary), 2. Enter "LogoLog1 solar.csv 5" in DOS, 3. The logger will then write data into solar.csv every 5 minutes. Hope this helps. I should consider making an English version.

Hello Superbrudi, I tried your method and it worked! Thank you so much! This logger opens up new possibilities for daily analysis. This forum is extremely valuable, and I'm glad to be here. [user_name]

Hi Superbrudi, I completed my first logging session, and it's impressive! Thanks again. I've been analyzing the results with Excel. The logging started at 9:00 AM and stopped automatically at 23:57. Is this normal, or did it stop because of a time change during the night? [user_name]
Hi [user_name], Your chart looks great. The logger should run continuously throughout the day. The interval options are 1, 2, 5, 10, 12, 15, 20, or 30 minutes.

Hi Superbrudi Superstar, Today I completed my second session on the laptop, but again, the logging stopped at 24:00. Is there a way to enable a 48-hour session instead of only 24 hours? Thank you, [user_name]

Hi [user_name], Please try this updated logger software. It's similar to the previous one, but the interval is now in seconds (0 to 65535 seconds). This software can log I1..I24, O1..O16, AI1..AI8, AO1..AO2, AM1..AM6.
Hi Superbrudi Superstar, I ran a new log session overnight using your latest software (LOGOCOM1), and it now successfully goes past 24:00, allowing unlimited logging time. Thanks so much! [user_name]

During my recent sessions, I noticed an asterisk "*" showing up on the [product_name] display near the date and time at each interval the logger software runs. This detail is helpful for confirming that logging is active and for checking the selected interval. Hi. [user_name]
Hi Superbrudi, I want to try your LogoLogger tool to record temperature data. Will it work with a USB PC cable? Thanks
Hello, I tried out this software and have a question. How do I create a PDF from the CSV file?

Hi [user_name], That's not directly related to [product_name]. You need PDF writing software such as PDFCreator. Download the program, then print the CSV file to PDF by selecting PDF as the printer. This approach works with any application that can print.

analysis.insight_summary: A user sought to record analog and digital data from their [product_name] over long sessions to analyze their solar heating system. Initial attempts with logger software were unsuccessful until guided by other community members, leading to success. The initial logging solution had a 24-hour limit, but after a software update, sessions could be extended indefinitely, resolving the issue.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants logging software that allows uninterrupted recording for 24–48 hours, capturing all necessary I/O data from [product_name], so they can perform detailed analysis in external tools like spreadsheets.
